ENUMA / TECHNICAL REPORT

Unifying Camera, Language, and Visual Controls
for Interactive World Modeling

Read abstract +

Interactive world models are evolving beyond camera-controlled navigation toward richer forms of user interaction, yet existing systems typically support only a limited subset of control signals. We present ENUMA, a unified interactive world model that jointly supports camera trajectories, language events, and visual references. Starting from a pretrained bidirectional video generator, we introduce dedicated conditioning mechanisms for heterogeneous controls, together with an interaction-oriented data curation pipeline and multi-task reinforcement learning to improve control fidelity.

To enable autoregressive deployment, we further propose Reference Forcing, which adapts the bidirectional model to chunk-wise causal generation with dynamically updated reference anchors and mixed forcing, and subsequently distills it into a four-step generator for efficient rollout. ENUMA supports causal generation up to 30 seconds and is evaluated on established world-model benchmarks, our proposed ENUMA-Bench, and direct human preference comparisons. Our results highlight heterogeneous interaction interfaces as a promising direction toward more general and continuously controllable world models.

Zhoujie Fu · Qing Yan · Yizhi Song · Zichuan Liu · Hao Kang · Yumin Jia · Xinyao Liao · Junyi Chen · Zixin Zhu · Zhexiao Xiong · Stathi Fotiadis · Jenson Yang · Jiamin Yuan · Guosheng Lin · Xin Lu
